jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.description:
Data Scientist – Autism Center of Excellence (ACE)

Department Overview

The University of Virginia's Autism Center of Excellence (ACE) is seeking a Data Scientist to support an NIH-funded Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) research project within the Department of Psychology.

The project involves the collection, management, and analysis of clinical, behavioral, neuroimaging, and other research data. The Data Scientist will collaborate with the ACE Data Coordinating Center (DCC), investigators, research coordinators, analysts, and information technology personnel to support secure and effective research data operations and scientific discovery.
Position Summary

The Data Scientist will oversee the secure, accurate, and efficient management of research data for an NIH-funded Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) project.

Working closely with the ACE Data Coordinating Center (DCC) Principal Investigator, this position will administer the project's REDCap-based data systems, coordinate user accounts and role-based permissions, and facilitate authorized access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources.

The successful candidate will ensure that clinical, behavioral, neuroimaging, and other study data are appropriately organized, quality controlled, documented, and managed in accordance with study protocols, institutional policies, NIH requirements, and applicable human-subjects and data-security standards.

In addition to research data management, this position will develop and apply modern data science, artificial intelligence (AI), and statistical approaches to analyze complex research datasets, generate meaningful visualizations, and support scientific publications and research outcomes.
Key Responsibilities

Research Data Management and REDCap Administration
• Administer and maintain the project's REDCap databases, including data collection forms, validation rules, user roles, permissions, audit trails, and routine system updates.
• Coordinate the creation, modification, periodic review, and deactivation of study user accounts, ensuring access is consistent with approved project roles and the principle of least privilege.
• Collaborate with research coordinators and study personnel to support data entry, troubleshoot database issues, monitor data completeness and consistency, and implement quality-assurance procedures.
• Develop and maintain data dictionaries, standard operating procedures, database documentation, access records, and other materials supporting reproducibility, regulatory compliance, and continuity of project operations.

Data Science, Statistical Analysis, and Artificial Intelligence
• Develop, validate, and apply modern data science and artificial intelligence computational approaches to clinical, behavioral, neuroimaging, and other ACE research data.
• Conduct formal statistical analyses to support research objectives and scientific investigations.
• Develop innovative data visualizations to communicate research findings and derived analytical results.
• Support reproducible analytical workflows, data processing, and preparation of research datasets for investigators and analysts.

Research Computing and Data Security
• Facilitate authorized access to institutional high-performance computing systems and related data-analysis environments in coordination with investigators, information technology staff, and system administrators.
• Support secure data transfers, dataset preparation, reporting, archiving, and data-sharing activities.
• Ensure research data practices align with Institutional Review Board (IRB) requirements, participant consent, NIH data-management and sharing expectations, and institutional privacy and security policies.
• Maintain appropriate documentation and access controls for sensitive research data.

Research Collaboration and Scientific Support
• Collaborate with project investigators, research coordinators, analysts, information technology personnel, and other stakeholders to support researc

jobs.title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks
jobs.description:
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

 

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

 

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

 

How it works

 

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
  3. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
  7. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

 

Requirements

 

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering
  • Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
  • Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
  • Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
  • Regular use of an AI coding tool
  • Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
  • At least 10 hours a week, starting now
  • A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

 

Nice to have

 

  • Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
  • Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

 

Terms

 

  • US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
  • The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
  • Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

 

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

Working closely with software, autonomy, simulation, and systems engineering teams, you will contribute to a high-assurance development environment focused on mission-critical reliability, rapid iteration, and engineering excellence. The ideal candidate has strong experience in Python-based automation, distributed systems testing, developer tooling, and modern CI/CD practices, along with an interest in autonomy, aerospace, robotics, or safety-critical software systems. Experience leveraging AI-assisted development and intelligent automation tools to accelerate testing, debugging, analytics, and developer productivity is highly valued.
